page: Amazon Web Services c9g.medium is a compute-optimized instance powered by an AWS Graviton Neoverse-V3 processor. Built on the arm64 architecture, this instance features 1 dedicated physical core and 1 vCPU running at 3.3 GHz. It is equipped with 2.0 GB of system memory, providing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The processor includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache, with hardware support for AES cryptography. No local storage or GPU hardware is bundled with this instance type, and it relies on a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals distinct performance characteristics for the single-core configuration. In single-threaded tasks, the instance demonstrates strong capabilities, achieving a top-tier rating in bzip3 decompression at 16.83 GB/sec and a strong rating in gzip compression at 36.12 GB/sec. However, because the instance is limited to a single vCPU, its multi-core stress-ng performance is poor, matching its single-core score of 1991.89. Memory bandwidth is also a constraint, with uncached large-block read speeds at 38.46 GB/sec and write speeds at 13.36 GB/sec, both falling into the weak and poor benchmark categories respectively.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c9g.medium offers a low-cost entry point to dedicated AWS Graviton9 Arm64 compute resources without the CPU credit limitations of burstable instances. The primary tradeoff is the highly constrained resource envelope, specifically the 2.0 GB memory limit and the single-threaded bottleneck, which makes it unsuitable for memory-intensive or highly parallelized applications. This server is best aligned with lightweight single-threaded workloads, basic web serving, microservices, utility scripting, and software compilation tasks that do not require multi-core execution.
